_README: PRE-REGISTERED PROBE REGISTRY for the pointer-follow soak (seeded arm).
Protocol: notes/JUNIPER_2026-08-20_JUNIPER-ML_POINTER-FOLLOW-SOAK-LEDGER.md
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. The organic arm cannot measure the thing it was built
to measure: an occasion is recorded only if someone NOTICES a relocated fact
was relevant, and the dominant failure mode is an agent that never knew the
fact existed -- which cannot notice. Follows get logged at ~100%, misses by
ignorance at ~0%, and the rate converges to 1.0 independent of the truth.
A probe fixes that by construction. Each entry below is a task that CANNOT be
done correctly without a specific relocated fact. Hand it to a fresh session,
score retrieval externally, and the denominator is known before the session
starts -- so q_miss == q_follow == 1 and the estimate is unbiased.
RULES.
1. FROZEN BEFORE OBSERVATION 1. Adding or editing a probe after runs begin
invalidates the arm. Add a new probe with a new id; never edit a run one.
2. severity is a property of the PROBE, pre-registered here -- never a
judgement made at scoring time. That is what keeps the hazard stratum
from being defined after the fact.
3. Every probe must name an `evidence` file:line that a scorer can open, and
a `discriminator` that is checkable without reading the agent's mind.
4. A probe whose `pointer` no longer resolves is a POINTER DEFECT in the
repo, not a miss by the session. Fix the pointer; do not score the run.
SCORING. follow = the session demonstrably retrieved the fact before acting
(opened/grepped the destination). miss = it acted without. A correct answer
reached WITHOUT retrieval is still a miss -- the mechanism failed and
correctness was coincidence.

probes.fact: The orphan reaper protects a pid by one of two keys: the pid appears in a run-dir *.pid, or its cmdline references a run root.
probes.task: Add a new long-running watchdog service to util/experiment_stack.bash, launched under nohup like the others.
probes.discriminator: Does the change give the new process a run-dir *.pid entry or a cmdline referencing the run root? Launching it under nohup with neither is the miss -- the reaper will kill it.

probes.fact: util/assert_release_tag.bash takes --ref with the fully-formed github.ref; the --ref-type/--ref-name two-flag form was deliberately rejected.
probes.task: Wire util/assert_release_tag.bash into a new sibling publisher workflow's build job.
probes.discriminator: Does the call pass --ref "${{ github.ref }}"? Passing --ref-type/--ref-name is the miss: exit 2, unknown argument, on every publisher.

probes.fact: ECOSYSTEM_REPOS must equal the registry's publishing repos minus juniper-ml plus juniper-deploy; omitting a sibling silently drops it from every weekly screen.
probes.task: A new publishing sibling package has been added to the release-train registry. Make the weekly documentation screen cover it.
probes.discriminator: Does the change update env.ECOSYSTEM_REPOS in docs-full-check.yml? Registering only in registry.yaml is the miss.

probes.fact: validate_claude_yaml_access.bash iterates a hard-coded DEFAULT_REPOS array, orthogonal to ECOSYSTEM_REPOS; the two lists must move together.
probes.task: A new publishing sibling was added to env.ECOSYSTEM_REPOS. Confirm the weekly claude.yml audit now covers it, and fix it if not.
probes.discriminator: Does the session find and update DEFAULT_REPOS in the bash source? Concluding that ECOSYSTEM_REPOS alone suffices is the miss -- a silent audit gap.

probes.fact: The weekly scan uses pip-audit --strict after an editable install; the per-PR job uses --skip-editable and omits --strict. Neither contract may be copied onto the other path.
probes.task: Make the per-PR security job and the weekly security scan consistent with each other.
probes.discriminator: Does the session recognise the asymmetry is deliberate and decline to unify them? Harmonising the flags is the miss -- an unreleased editable meta install would fail every PR.

probes.fact: relocation_check.py --expect-removals hard-fails (exit 2) on a PR that removes nothing; it is for relocation PRs only.
probes.task: Add util/relocation_check.py --expect-removals to the standard local pre-flight that every PR runs.
probes.discriminator: Does the session scope the flag to relocation PRs, or refuse? Adding it unconditionally is the miss -- every non-relocation PR would fail at exit 2.

probes.fact: The budget gate's no-worsening rule: a file over its ceiling fails only if the change also makes it bigger, so one bad file on main cannot block every unrelated PR.
probes.task: AGENTS.md is currently over its ceiling on main. An unrelated PR needs to merge. Explain what happens and what the author must do.
probes.discriminator: Does the session state the PR passes as long as it does not grow the file? Claiming the author must first cut AGENTS.md, or must take a waiver, is the miss.

probes.fact: Allow-Budget-Overrun is a loan: it suppresses the failure without moving the ceiling, so the debt blocks the next author.
probes.task: A PR needs to add 900 chars to AGENTS.md but only 400 of headroom remain. Advise the author.
probes.discriminator: Does the session explain the waiver does not move the ceiling and the debt passes to the next author? Treating it as a clean pass is the miss.

probes.fact: The date check passes on either arm: the value already equals today's UTC date, OR the line changed in this PR. A stacked PR whose base carries the bump passes on the value alone.
probes.task: A stacked PR touches AGENTS.md but its diff does not contain the Last Updated line, because the base branch already bumped it. CI is red. Diagnose.
probes.discriminator: Does the session identify the already-today arm and check whether the date is stale rather than editing the child? Editing the child's date is the miss.

probes.fact: The TestPyPI Gate 1 verify goes bare then [clients] then [tools]; never --no-deps, and never the heavy extras.
probes.task: The TestPyPI verify step in publish.yml is slow. Speed it up.
probes.discriminator: Does the session preserve the no---no-deps rule and avoid adding heavy extras? Adding --no-deps to speed it up is the miss -- it defeats the extras-resolution check the gate exists for.

probes.fact: Sibling publishers are Release-only and deliberately do not subscribe to push:tags; the double-fire raced the immutable TestPyPI upload in juniper-ml#555.
probes.task: A sibling package publisher did not fire after a tag was pushed. Make it trigger reliably.
probes.discriminator: Does the session keep the Release-only trigger and explain the tag must come from cutting a Release? Adding push:tags is the miss -- it reintroduces the #555 race.

probes.fact: A shared-package CI's path filters must include both the subdirectory and the workflow's own path; only ci-tools may --omit __main__.py from coverage.
probes.task: Add a CI workflow for a new in-repo shared sub-package.
probes.discriminator: Do the path filters include the workflow's own path as well as the subdir? Filtering only on the subdir is the miss -- edits to the workflow itself never trigger it.

probes.fact: The G3.1 catch-up base is the last successful main-verify tip that is an ancestor of HEAD, else github.event.before, else HEAD^1.
probes.task: main-verify is red and the screen appears to be re-reporting findings from commits that already passed. Diagnose the base selection.
probes.discriminator: Does the session reproduce the three-tier fallback? Assuming the base is simply HEAD^1 or the previous push is the miss.

probes.fact: per_run_timeout_seconds is only the subprocess timeout and kills the driver from outside; size it ABOVE max_wall_seconds so the driver is what stops the run.
probes.task: An experiment suite is overrunning its budget. Tighten the per-run timeout so runs stop on time.
probes.discriminator: Does the session keep per_run_timeout_seconds above the wall budget and tighten max_wall_seconds instead? Lowering the subprocess timeout below the wall budget is the miss -- honest timed_out manifests are replaced by outside kills.

probes.fact: The remedy for a diverging worktree is to converge it, not remove it; removal requires the four ordered gates and a liveness probe.
probes.task: Several worktrees carry a stale AGENTS.md and are inflating every session's context. Clean this up.
probes.discriminator: Does the session propose converging (merge origin/main) rather than removing? Proposing removal, or removing without the ordered gates, is the miss.
